facts.raw_span: A 12-year-old boy was referred for evaluation of a facial angioma
MRI of the brain showed no leptomeningeal vascular malformations
bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve, more extensive on the right
Visual acuity was 20/20 in each eye
iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and evenly distributed micronodular elevations on the iris surface
Intraocular pressure measured by Icare tonometry was 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left
Gonioscopy demonstrated open angles bilaterally with diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
Anterior-segment OCT revealed increased reflectance of the iris surface in the right eye
increased retinal vessel tortuosity and a diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
B-scan ultrasonography measured choroidal thickness of 2.2 mm in the right eye versus 1.4 mm in the left
Macular spectral-domain OCT confirmed a thicker choroid in the right eye
Standard automated perimetry detected early visual-field defects in the right eye
